headline: Weekend wrap: desks say the AI flush is late-stage (retail puke, PB net at summer lows) but nobody is re-grossing yet, and the one live rotation is long hyperscalers, short neoclouds and picks-and-shovels.
market_read: Weekend desk wraps agree the post-midterm week was a de-leveraging event in AI rather than a regime change, but they split on timing. UBS (Ruple, 7 Nov) has PB net exposure to AI winners back at summer-unwind/Liberation Day lows and SOX puts being monetised; Vanda (Liu, 7 Nov) calls Thursday the largest retail puke in its dataset, which historically marks a drawdown's final stage; JPM's Schlegel (via See, 8 Nov) says HF semis selling hit 4z yet the TPM flow trigger for capitulation has not fired, and JPM's Silver (8 Nov) doubts HFs re-gross before Christmas. Inside AI the flow is a rotation, not an exit: UBS's TMT desk saw hyperscalers bought with neocloud supply, Bernstein's desk (Doran) saw neoclouds, semis and hardware sold with short-sale tickets rising, and GS's Pasquariello (7 Nov) reads the week as 'arguably better for the hyperscalers, but worse most everywhere else'. A fresh Friday negative is MSFT winding down its Oracle capacity deal (Bloomberg via UBS), with ORCL CDS wider.

up.why: UBS's TMT desk (Ruple, 7 Nov) names buying hyperscalers funded by neocloud sales as the week's biggest flow; Bernstein's spec sales (Seidman, 7 Nov) carries MSFT as a 'safety' idea (Azure +600bp vs a 300bp bogey, FCF-positive FY27) and reports investors do not see it as a funding-flow headwind; stepping back from risky DC projects and the Oracle rental deal reads as capex discipline. Monitor: no MSFT analog band or Bloomberg-X move in monitor.json (through 6 Nov), so this is desk evidence only. 1-5 days: the rotation can persist while semis stay under systematic supply into Monday. 2-4 weeks: depends on whether 'less buildout = better hyperscaler FCF' holds as the narrative.
up.confirm: Hyperscalers outperform SOX on Monday-Tuesday; more desks report long-only buying of MSFT/AMZN.
up.weaken: A broad AI bid returns and money rotates back into semis; or MSFT capex guide-downs get read as weak demand rather than discipline.

up.why: Bernstein's spec sales (7 Nov): AWS +39% with 40%+ seen in 2027/28 driving EPS revisions, Alexa for Shopping easing the horizontal-agent overhang, re:Invent as a catalyst; UBS's desk has hyperscalers bought; JPM Asia (Hariharan, 8 Nov) says Alchip guides Trainium3 revenue >100% in 2027. Offsetting: Bernstein research has AMZN the most exposed to restrictive states (already logged 7 Nov). Monitor: no AMZN analog or Bloomberg-X move (through 6 Nov). 1-5 days: rotation beneficiary; 2-4 weeks: re:Invent (early Dec) is the named catalyst.
up.confirm: re:Invent agent/Trainium news; Texas or other states' rules spare under-construction capacity.
up.weaken: State permitting rules hit AWS's planned sites, or agentic-commerce fears return.

up.why: Bloomberg-X attention is falling (dz -2.05, 7-day avg 698 vs 888 over 28 days) while the stock is +2.3% over 7 days, and Bernstein's spec sales (7 Nov) says the market sees AI in Search as 'when, not if' at a low-to-mid 20x multiple; also in UBS's hyperscaler bid. Monitor: HOT 42 and BULL 46.6, both in the 40-60 band; in GOOG's own history the HOT 40-60 band was followed by a +1.4% median 5-session move (67.5% up, n=40) and +0.2% over 10 sessions. 2-4 weeks: Search monetisation evidence is still the gate.
up.confirm: Attention stays quiet while price holds above the pre-midterm level.
up.weaken: Another Search-share scare or a GCP capacity delay in restrictive states.

up.why: JPM's Euro TMT specialist (Silver, 8 Nov) calls ASML, ASM International and Nokia increasingly compelling on valuation with attractive 2027 growth, and expects investors to come back once positioning is flushed; Jefferies Europe (via Beavington, 7 Nov) says an ASML visit showed strong demand. Divergence: the same Jefferies team says it is too early to bottom-fish semis, and Bernstein's desk flags WFE expectations as too hot. Monitor: no ASML analog band or Bloomberg-X move. 1-5 days: no catalyst; 2-4 weeks: AMAT (Thu) and ONTO (Mon) CY27 commentary set the WFE tone.
up.confirm: AMAT guides CY27 WFE up strongly and semicap holds while SOX retests.
up.weaken: AMAT/ONTO cautious on CY27, or DDR5 spot weakness spreads to memory capex.

down.why: Friday's headline that MSFT is winding down its deal to rent AI capacity from Oracle (Bloomberg, via UBS's Ruple, 7 Nov): ORCL can re-let it, possibly at higher prices, but its dependence on the AI labs rises and ORCL CDS widened, after a week in which the ledger already had ORCL's ~$20bn bond+equity raise weighing (Rothschild desk, 3 Nov). Monitor: no ORCL analog band or Bloomberg-X move (through 6 Nov, before the headline). 1-5 days: credit-led; 2-4 weeks: whether the capacity is re-contracted.
down.confirm: ORCL CDS keeps widening (check AI_Credit_Live), or another hyperscaler steps back from OCI.
down.weaken: Oracle announces the capacity re-let to a lab at better pricing.

down.why: Three sources point the same way: UBS's TMT desk saw neoclouds sold to fund hyperscaler buys, Bernstein's desk (Doran) saw neoclouds sold on Thursday with short-sale tickets rising, and Vanda (7 Nov) says neocloud credit spreads keep widening. CRWV reports next week. Monitor: HOT 36.8 and BULL 33.8 (20-40 band); in CRWV's own short history the HOT 20-40 band saw a +11.9% median 5-session move but -4.7% over 10 sessions (n=5, too small to lean on). 1-5 days: print-driven; 2-4 weeks: funding/credit is the swing factor.
down.confirm: Print shows backlog slippage or financing on worse terms; spreads widen further.
down.weaken: Contracted-through-2027 capacity (Bernstein, 6 Nov) and a clean print trigger short covering.

down.why: Part of the same neocloud supply UBS's desk (7 Nov) saw funding hyperscaler buys; NBIS also reports next week. Monitor: no NBIS analog band or Bloomberg-X move. Lower conviction than CRWV: one desk source only.
down.confirm: Desks report further neocloud selling into the print.
down.weaken: Print shows capacity additions on schedule outside restrictive states.

down.why: UBS's desk (7 Nov) reads LITE's willingness to sell to MRVL as a peak-cycle signal and a sentiment overhang, with both stocks lower; divergent view: Jefferies' NDR (logged 7 Nov, repeated in the Saturday daily) says scale-in production targets moved to 2028-29 and reiterates BUY on both. MRVL monitor: HOT 72.3 (60-80 band, n=2, not usable). 1-5 days: deal-spread trading; 2-4 weeks: whether optical scale-in timing gets confirmed by customers.
down.confirm: Spread widens further or holders vote against.
down.weaken: A customer confirms 2028 optical scale-in volumes.

down.why: UBS's desk (7 Nov) lists DDOG among software names that missed or guided lower. Monitor: Bloomberg-X attention spiked (dz +2.28, 7-day avg 43 vs 8 over 28 days) as the stock fell 23.5% in 7 days; HOT 79.6 (60-80 band) was followed in DDOG's own history by a -3.0% median 5-session move (40% up, n=10). This is attention on a falling stock, not crowding.
down.confirm: Attention stays high while price fails to bounce with the tape.
down.weaken: Software rallies as the 'AI losers' relief trade JPM's Silver describes.

themes.title: Rotation inside AI: hyperscalers bought, picks-and-shovels and neoclouds sold
themes.text: UBS's TMT desk (Ruple, 7 Nov) and Bernstein's desk (Doran via Seidman, 7 Nov) describe the same flow from both sides: buying hyperscalers, selling neoclouds, semis and hardware, with short-sale tickets rising. GS's Pasquariello (7 Nov, desk commentary) frames the new fact set as better for the hyperscalers and worse for the rest of the AI infrastructure complex, with less upside convexity in picks-and-shovels. The read-across: a slower buildout is being treated as FCF-positive for the spenders and negative for the suppliers.

themes.title: Washout or capitulation? Desks disagree on timing
themes.text: Late-stage camp: Vanda (Liu, 7 Nov) says Thursday's retail selling was the largest in its dataset and such episodes nearly always mark a drawdown's final stage, with CTA selling near complete; UBS (7 Nov) has PB net AI exposure at summer lows. Not-yet camp: JPM's Schlegel (via See, 8 Nov) says positioning reset but the TPM flow trigger for capitulation has not fired; JPM's Silver (8 Nov) expects HFs to run low gross into year-end; Jefferies Europe (7 Nov) says it is too early to bottom-fish semis while Jefferies US says build a holiday shopping list. Weighting: these are desk and flow-strategy views, not rated research.

themes.title: SemiAnalysis in Inner Mongolia: the China contrast to the Texas backlash
themes.text: SemiAnalysis (Tan, Ontiveros, Laoban, Patel, 7 Nov; preview read) visited Envision's Galaxy campus in Ulanqab, planned for up to 800 MW of IT capacity, whose first 120 MW phase was delivered within a year at about a fifth of US cost, with a 5 MW hall running SST-native 800V DC. It contrasts China's accelerating build with Texas's anti-datacenter sentiment. 800V is a separate debate; these MW are IT capacity at one campus and should not be mixed with US facility-GW figures. No universe-company observation logged.

themes.title: WFE: desk says too hot, research says beat/raise
themes.text: Bernstein's spec sales (7 Nov) lists 'WFE expectations running too hot' among the negative themes of the cycle, while Jefferies' US team (via Beavington, 7 Nov) expects AMAT to beat/raise with revenue guided HSD+ vs consensus +5%, and peers point to 30%+ WFE growth next year. AMAT (Thu) and ONTO (Mon) are the tests.
